svg.title: Layer_Dense with forward and backward methods, and what each one caches
svg.desc: A hand-drawn class blueprint. On the left, a card for class Layer_Dense holds its two methods side by side at equal size. The forward method caches self.inputs, marked with a coloured spine, then computes self.output as inputs matrix-multiplied by the weights plus the biases; a note records that the cache line is the only addition to the Part 04 class and that without it backward has nothing to multiply by. The backward method computes self.dweights from the transposed cached inputs times dvalues, self.dbiases from a sum along the batch axis with keepdims, and self.dinputs from dvalues times the transposed weights; a note records that it reads the cache on its first line and writes three arrays without returning anything. Three cards on the right receive them: dweights of shape n_inputs by n_neurons and dbiases of shape one by n_neurons both go to the optimiser, and dinputs of shape N by n_inputs goes to the previous layer.
svg.text: One cached array in forward, three gradients out of backward. That is the whole contract of a layer.
The cache line is the only
Every class with a backward caches something in its forward. Layer_Dense caches its inputs; ReLU caches its inputs too.
The cost is one array reference per layer, held until the backward pass has used it.
